key_insight: This paper moves cross-view object geo-localization beyond simple 2D appearance matching by introducing a geometry-aware, single-stage framework. It pairs a large, high-fidelity building dataset with a unified model that leverages spatial structure for more reliable localization across ground, drone, and satellite views.
problem_solved: The paper tackles the challenge of locating an object in geo-tagged reference imagery from a different viewpoint, especially when existing methods are limited by weak geometric reasoning, sparse datasets, missing metadata, and non-standard field-of-view images.
method: Introduces a large-scale building dataset with rich geometric and cross-view information to support more realistic CVOGL training and evaluation.
Proposes a unified single-stage framework that directly aligns query and reference views while incorporating geometry-aware cues, rather than depending only on 2D feature matching.
Designed to better handle diverse prompts and view changes, improving robustness in cross-view localization scenarios.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work offers a more practical foundation for cross-view localization by combining stronger supervision data with a more physically grounded model. It can improve performance in remote sensing, robotics, navigation, and any application requiring object localization across viewpoints.

paper_title: Beyond 2D Matching: A Unified Single-Stage Framework for Geometry-Aware Cross-View Object Geo-Localization
paper_authors: Liyao Wang, Ruipu Wu, Haojun Xu, Lei Shi, Linjiang Huang
